question: Show the top 10 customers by total payment amount
sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, SUM(p.amount) AS total_paid FROM customer c JOIN payment p ON c.customer_id = p.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name ORDER BY total_paid DESC LIMIT 10

question: Which films were rented the most times?
sql: SELECT f.title, COUNT(r.rental_id) AS rental_count FROM film f JOIN inventory i ON f.film_id = i.film_id JOIN rental r ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id GROUP BY f.film_id, f.title ORDER BY rental_count DESC LIMIT 10

question: List all actors who appeared in more than 30 films
sql: SELECT a.actor_id, a.first_name, a.last_name, COUNT(fa.film_id) AS film_count FROM actor a JOIN film_actor fa ON a.actor_id = fa.actor_id GROUP BY a.actor_id, a.first_name, a.last_name HAVING COUNT(fa.film_id) > 30 ORDER BY film_count DESC

question: What are the total sales per store?
sql: SELECT s.store_id, ci.city, SUM(p.amount) AS total_sales FROM store s JOIN address a ON s.address_id = a.address_id JOIN city ci ON a.city_id = ci.city_id JOIN staff st ON s.store_id = st.store_id JOIN payment p ON st.staff_id = p.staff_id GROUP BY s.store_id, ci.city ORDER BY total_sales DESC

question: Which customers currently have a rental that has not been returned yet?
sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, COUNT(*) AS unreturned_rentals FROM customer c JOIN rental r ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id WHERE r.return_date IS NULL GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name ORDER BY unreturned_rentals DESC, c.customer_id

question: How many films are in each category?
sql: SELECT cat.name AS category, COUNT(fc.film_id) AS film_count FROM category cat JOIN film_category fc ON cat.category_id = fc.category_id GROUP BY cat.name ORDER BY film_count DESC

question: Show average film length by rating
sql: SELECT rating, ROUND(AVG(length), 1) AS avg_length_minutes, COUNT(*) AS film_count FROM film GROUP BY rating ORDER BY avg_length_minutes DESC

question: Which staff member processed the most rentals?
sql: SELECT s.staff_id, s.first_name, s.last_name, COUNT(r.rental_id) AS rental_count FROM staff s JOIN rental r ON s.staff_id = r.staff_id GROUP BY s.staff_id, s.first_name, s.last_name ORDER BY rental_count DESC

question: Show the top 3 customers by revenue in each country
sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, co.country, SUM(p.amount) AS total_paid, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY co.country ORDER BY SUM(p.amount) DESC) AS rn FROM customer c JOIN payment p ON c.customer_id = p.customer_id JOIN address a ON c.address_id = a.address_id JOIN city ci ON a.city_id = ci.city_id JOIN country co ON ci.country_id = co.country_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, co.country) SELECT customer_id, first_name, last_name, country, total_paid FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 3 ORDER BY country, total_paid DESC

question: Which actors have appeared in both Horror and Comedy films?
sql: SELECT a.actor_id, a.first_name, a.last_name FROM actor a JOIN film_actor fa ON a.actor_id = fa.actor_id JOIN film_category fc ON fa.film_id = fc.film_id JOIN category c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id WHERE c.name = 'Horror' INTERSECT SELECT a.actor_id, a.first_name, a.last_name FROM actor a JOIN film_actor fa ON a.actor_id = fa.actor_id JOIN film_category fc ON fa.film_id = fc.film_id JOIN category c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id WHERE c.name = 'Comedy'

question: Show monthly rental counts for the year 2005
sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', rental_date) AS month, COUNT(*) AS rental_count FROM rental WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM rental_date) = 2005 GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', rental_date) ORDER BY month

question: What is the cumulative revenue over time by month?
sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', payment_date) AS month, SUM(amount) AS revenue FROM payment GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', payment_date)) SELECT month, revenue, SUM(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS cumulative_revenue FROM monthly ORDER BY month

question: Find customers who rented more than the average number of rentals
sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, COUNT(r.rental_id) AS rental_count FROM customer c JOIN rental r ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name HAVING COUNT(r.rental_id) > (SELECT AVG(cnt) FROM (SELECT COUNT(rental_id) AS cnt FROM rental GROUP BY customer_id) sub) ORDER BY rental_count DESC

question: Compare average payment amount per customer across stores
sql: SELECT s.store_id, ci.city, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS customer_count, ROUND(AVG(p.amount), 2) AS avg_payment FROM store s JOIN address a ON s.address_id = a.address_id JOIN city ci ON a.city_id = ci.city_id JOIN customer c ON c.store_id = s.store_id JOIN payment p ON p.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY s.store_id, ci.city ORDER BY store_id

question: Which films have never been rented?
sql: SELECT f.film_id, f.title, f.rating FROM film f WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM inventory i JOIN rental r ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id WHERE i.film_id = f.film_id) ORDER BY f.title

question: Show the top 5 most profitable film categories by total rental revenue
sql: SELECT cat.name AS category, SUM(p.amount) AS total_revenue, COUNT(r.rental_id) AS total_rentals FROM category cat JOIN film_category fc ON cat.category_id = fc.category_id JOIN film f ON fc.film_id = f.film_id JOIN inventory i ON f.film_id = i.film_id JOIN rental r ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id JOIN payment p ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id GROUP BY cat.name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 5

question: For each city, show how many customers have rented Action films
sql: SELECT ci.city, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS action_renters FROM city ci JOIN address a ON ci.city_id = a.city_id JOIN customer c ON a.address_id = c.address_id JOIN rental r ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id JOIN film_category fc ON i.film_id = fc.film_id JOIN category cat ON fc.category_id = cat.category_id WHERE cat.name = 'Action' GROUP BY ci.city ORDER BY action_renters DESC

question: Rank actors by their total rental revenue across all their films
sql: SELECT a.actor_id, a.first_name, a.last_name, SUM(p.amount) AS total_revenue, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(p.amount) DESC) AS revenue_rank FROM actor a JOIN film_actor fa ON a.actor_id = fa.actor_id JOIN inventory i ON fa.film_id = i.film_id JOIN rental r ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id JOIN payment p ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id GROUP BY a.actor_id, a.first_name, a.last_name ORDER BY revenue_rank LIMIT 20

question: What is the average rental duration in days for each film category?
sql: SELECT cat.name AS category, ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (r.return_date - r.rental_date)) / 86400)::numeric, 2) AS avg_rental_days FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id JOIN film_category fc ON i.film_id = fc.film_id JOIN category cat ON fc.category_id = cat.category_id WHERE r.return_date IS NOT NULL GROUP BY cat.category_id, cat.name ORDER BY avg_rental_days DESC

question: Which actors appeared in Action films but never in Horror films?
sql: SELECT a.actor_id, a.first_name, a.last_name FROM actor a JOIN film_actor fa ON a.actor_id = fa.actor_id JOIN film_category fc ON fa.film_id = fc.film_id JOIN category c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id WHERE c.name = 'Action' EXCEPT SELECT a.actor_id, a.first_name, a.last_name FROM actor a JOIN film_actor fa ON a.actor_id = fa.actor_id JOIN film_category fc ON fa.film_id = fc.film_id JOIN category c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id WHERE c.name = 'Horror'

question: What percentage of total revenue does each film category contribute?
sql: SELECT cat.name AS category, SUM(p.amount) AS revenue, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(p.amount) / SUM(SUM(p.amount)) OVER (), 2) AS pct_of_total FROM payment p JOIN rental r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id JOIN film_category fc ON i.film_id = fc.film_id JOIN category cat ON fc.category_id = cat.category_id GROUP BY cat.category_id, cat.name ORDER BY revenue DESC

question: Show month over month revenue change
sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', payment_date) AS month, SUM(amount) AS revenue FROM payment GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', payment_date)) SELECT month, revenue, revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS change_vs_prev_month, ROUND(100.0 * (revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month)) / NULLIF(LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month), 0), 2) AS pct_change FROM monthly ORDER BY month

question: For each category, which film was rented the most?
sql: WITH film_rentals AS (SELECT cat.category_id, cat.name AS category, f.film_id, f.title, COUNT(r.rental_id) AS rental_count FROM category cat JOIN film_category fc ON cat.category_id = fc.category_id JOIN film f ON fc.film_id = f.film_id JOIN inventory i ON f.film_id = i.film_id JOIN rental r ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id GROUP BY cat.category_id, cat.name, f.film_id, f.title), ranked AS (SELECT *, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category_id ORDER BY rental_count DESC) AS rnk FROM film_rentals) SELECT category, title, rental_count FROM ranked WHERE rnk = 1 ORDER BY category, title

question: How many customers were created each year?
sql: SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM create_date)::int AS year, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM customer GROUP BY EXTRACT(YEAR FROM create_date) ORDER BY year

question: Find films with 'academy' in the title
sql: SELECT film_id, title, release_year FROM film WHERE title ILIKE '%academy%' ORDER BY title

question: Which film categories have an average film length above the overall average length?
sql: SELECT cat.name AS category, ROUND(AVG(f.length), 1) AS avg_length FROM category cat JOIN film_category fc ON cat.category_id = fc.category_id JOIN film f ON fc.film_id = f.film_id GROUP BY cat.category_id, cat.name HAVING AVG(f.length) > (SELECT AVG(length) FROM film) ORDER BY avg_length DESC

question: Which customers have rented films from every category?
sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name FROM customer c JOIN rental r ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id JOIN film_category fc ON i.film_id = fc.film_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT fc.category_id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM category) ORDER BY c.customer_id

question: What is the longest film in each rating?
sql: SELECT rating, title, length FROM (SELECT rating, title, length, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY rating ORDER BY length DESC) AS rnk FROM film) t WHERE rnk = 1 ORDER BY rating, title

question: How many films does each actor appear in, and who has the most?
sql: SELECT a.actor_id, a.first_name, a.last_name, COUNT(DISTINCT fa.film_id) AS film_count FROM actor a JOIN film_actor fa ON a.actor_id = fa.actor_id GROUP BY a.actor_id, a.first_name, a.last_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT fa.film_id) = (SELECT MAX(cnt) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM film_actor GROUP BY actor_id) m) ORDER BY a.actor_id

question: Which customers spent more than the average customer?
sql: WITH spend AS (SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, SUM(p.amount) AS total FROM customer c JOIN payment p ON c.customer_id = p.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name) SELECT customer_id, first_name, last_name, total FROM spend WHERE total > (SELECT AVG(total) FROM spend) ORDER BY total DESC, customer_id

question: On average, how many films does each actor appear in?
sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(n)::numeric, 2) AS avg_films_per_actor FROM (SELECT a.actor_id, COUNT(fa.film_id) AS n FROM actor a LEFT JOIN film_actor fa ON fa.actor_id = a.actor_id GROUP BY a.actor_id) t
